races.name: British EBF Fillies' Novice Stakes (GBB/GBBPlus Race)
PD Hook Gallop Handicap

runners_data.name: Simba's Pride
runners_data.note: Lightly raced 3yo in good recent form (two wins and a second from last four on Good ground at this trip), prominent racer for in-form Michael Dods; only 4 days since last run but Dods regularly runs horses in quick succession with success, and this flat course and Good ground suits perfectly.

runners_data.name: Dragon Spin
runners_data.note: Showed a win and three places from five starts at 5f, so the trip and trip record are solid; however, this is a genuine hold-up horse that has been mapped to midfield because the field is stacked with closers — it will likely race further back than shown and needs pace to collapse rather than merely ease.

runners_data.name: Golden Havana
runners_data.note: All five career runs have come on Tapeta at Southwell (one win, two thirds), so this Good turf surface is a significant and unproven switch; Connor Beasley's booking is competent but the form basis is entirely on a different surface, making this runner the biggest unknown in the field.

runners_data.name: Ice Cold Alex
runners_data.note: Listed as a non-runner — disregard for race shape purposes; was a true hold-up type with a moderate record on Good ground in any case.

runners_data.name: U Turn
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with a winning run on Good ground at 5f to his name, but a 276-day absence is a major flag for a 3yo who has not run since last season; Tim Easterby does place runners from a lay-off, and David Allan's booking suggests fitness is believed, but the fitness risk is real.

runners_data.name: Riffa Spirit
runners_data.note: Wears a tongue-tie and has shown ability to win at 6f on Standard, and has placed at 5f on Good; the key caveat is that this is a natural hold-up runner forced into a busier midfield, and at 22 days since last run with an apprentice aboard, it faces a tough ask to get a clear run.

runners_data.name: Arlo's Girl
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner and sole pace-setter in this race — she should clear to the front immediately; her highest OR of 74 gives her weight to carry and recent form shows a win on Standard but disappointing efforts since, including an 8th on Good ground, which tempers confidence that a solo lead automatically translates to victory.

runners_data.name: Bravo Hotel
runners_data.note: Consistent 3yo with five placed efforts from five visible runs (three on Good, two on Soft), giving her a solid profile on this going; 258 days off is a concern, but Michael & David Easterby are no strangers to placing horses fresh, and Joanna Mason is an experienced hand — her stamina-friendly hold-up style may suit if the pace is honest enough.

races.paceDynamic: Arlo's Girl is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, she should coast to the front unchallenged and set a controlled, honest gallop on Good ground over this flat Thirsk 5f. Simba's Pride and U Turn will press from prominent positions just behind, creating a compact early shape rather than an all-out pace battle. This field holds more hold-up types than the map can accommodate at the rear — Riffa Spirit, Dragon Spin, and Golden Havana are true hold-up horses forced into a midfield mapping, and all three are likely to find their natural ground further back than their charted positions suggest, meaning they will need something to go wrong up front to get involved. The race shape — an uncontested leader, honest but unblazed pace, and a cluster of prominent runners just behind — strongly favours prominent racers who can track the leader and pounce in the final furlong; true closers will find the tempo insufficient to reel in those already positioned close to the pace.

scenarios.title: Controlled lead, prominent pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Arlo's Girl dictates from the front without serious pressure and the prominent pair track her into the straight.
scenarios.body: If Arlo's Girl dictates from the front without serious pressure and the prominent pair track her into the straight.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Leader holds on uncontested
scenarios.trigger: If Arlo's Girl finds an even more comfortable lead than expected and the chasers fail to close the gap.
scenarios.body: If Arlo's Girl finds an even more comfortable lead than expected and the chasers fail to close the gap.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-up horses land late
scenarios.trigger: If the early gallop is faster than expected and the front two fade badly in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: If the early gallop is faster than expected and the front two fade badly in the final furlong.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Carnage in the pack
scenarios.trigger: If crowding or interference disrupts the midfield group and reshuffles the finish.
scenarios.body: If crowding or interference disrupts the midfield group and reshuffles the finish.

watchPoints.text: Arlo's Girl breaks cleanly — if she misses the break even fractionally, the entire race shape collapses and prominent horses Simba's Pride and U Turn could inherit the lead with a far harder race to control.

U Turn's 276-day absence is the single biggest fitness risk in the race; watch the pre-race market move — if he drifts significantly in betting, connections may have doubts, which would materially reduce the probability of Scenario A playing out as mapped.

Golden Havana's switch from Tapeta to Good turf is untested across all five career starts; if she handles the surface change, her Dods yard form counts, but any greenness or unfamiliarity with turf movement could see her outpaced early and irrelevant.

Bravo Hotel's layoff (258 days) combined with a hold-up style means watch how cleanly she gets away — in a tight 8-runner field on a flat track, any early scrimmaging in midfield could cost her the clear passage she needs to make her consistent placed form count.

races.name: Theakston Brewing Legends Since 1827 Handicap

runners_data.name: Kings Merchant
runners_data.note: Philip Kirby hold-up type with 18 days' rest and a poor recent record on Good ground (0 wins from 10 similar-going runs); naturally races at the rear but the crowded hold-up division means it may be forced wider mid-division, further reducing its already slim prospects.

runners_data.name: Pull The Rug
runners_data.note: Connor Beasley rides this 3yo for Edward Bethell, whose yard is in decent form (T14: 3/23); a genuine hold-up performer that won on Soft last time, but Good ground (0 wins from 5 similar runs) and a 6f trip are likely to be stretching its effectiveness here.

runners_data.name: Record Day
runners_data.note: Brian Ellison 3yo with a concerning fade note on finishing, only one run on Good-comparable ground from four, and naturally a hold-up type that will be competing for rear positions in a busy back-section — its recent form figures of 8489 do not inspire confidence in any scenario.

runners_data.name: Harlequin Bay
runners_data.note: Fahey-trained 3yo who has placed twice on Soft/Standard but recorded just one run on Good ground (finishing 5th), and whose natural hold-up tendency means it joins a congested group of closers unlikely to find clear air in a steadily-run race.

runners_data.name: Sugar Baby
runners_data.note: Veteran 8yo who has won three times on Good ground over 6f (3W from 11 similar-going runs) and races prominently, giving Mark Winn a natural tactical position to press Space Bear; the 134lb burden is a significant weight concern but the proven Good-ground form is a real angle.

runners_data.name: Frantic
runners_data.note: Ed Walker's lightly-raced 3yo has been placed second in all four Good or Good-equivalent starts and races prominently; George Downing should get a clean view behind Space Bear, and the consistency of the placed form at 6f on this going makes it a natural beneficiary of a sensibly-paced race.

runners_data.name: Tactical Formation
runners_data.note: Jack Garritty partners this Fahey 3yo returning from 166 days off — a significant concern — and the horse's style is uncertain (U); two previous placed efforts on Good ground offer some encouragement but the lengthy absence is a major flag against it being fully wound up.

runners_data.name: Taygar
runners_data.note: Michael Dods' 5yo has an exceptional record at 6f on Good ground (14 runs, 7 places, all on this going) and is a consistent placed performer for Sean Kirrane; a true hold-up type competing in a crowded rear-division means it must find a gap late in a race that may not produce a strong enough closing pace to reward it.

runners_data.name: Emperor Caradoc
runners_data.note: David Nolan rides this Paul Midgley 7yo who has three wins and five places from 11 similar-going runs and won at 6f on Good ground recently; a natural hold-up performer with real course-and-distance form, it is the most credible closer in the field if any gap appears late.

runners_data.name: Vingegaard
runners_data.note: Julie Camacho's 4yo carries a hood (hg:b) and has some Good-ground placed form (0W, 2P from 7 similar runs) but Ryan Sexton faces a challenge getting a clean run from the hold-up position in a race where Space Bear is likely to control a measured tempo.

runners_data.name: Space Bear
runners_data.note: Michael Appleby's 3yo is the lone front-runner in this field and Joanna Mason should be able to stride into a comfortable lead from the off; one win on Good ground from three similar runs, and while the STYLE_FIT tag acknowledges the style mismatch in context, the absence of any rival willing or able to seriously test it early is its biggest asset today.

races.paceDynamic: Space Bear is the lone confirmed front-runner and, with no serious challenger for the lead at the top of the field, Joanna Mason can dictate from the front at a sustainable, even gallop on Good ground over 6f at Thirsk. The field contains a significant cluster of genuine hold-up types — Kings Merchant, Record Day, Harlequin Bay, and Taygar are all natural closers who cannot all find their preferred rear position; some will be shuffled into midfield against their instinct, which dilutes their effectiveness late. Frantic and Sugar Baby will look to press Space Bear from a prominent position, but neither is a natural front-runner and neither is likely to force a genuinely testing early tempo. With a controlled, single-paced gallop the most probable outcome, horses who travel prominently or who are effective from a mid-division position in a steadily-run sprint will be best placed — true deep closers face a compromised scenario, as the lack of pressure from the front means there will be little pace to close into.

scenarios.title: Space Bear Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Space Bear is allowed to stride into an uncontested lead and dictates a sustainable gallop throughout.
scenarios.body: If Space Bear is allowed to stride into an uncontested lead and dictates a sustainable gallop throughout.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Battle Late
scenarios.trigger: If Frantic or Sugar Baby press Space Bear hard enough to force a stronger tempo, setting up a finish between the front two positions.
scenarios.body: If Frantic or Sugar Baby press Space Bear hard enough to force a stronger tempo, setting up a finish between the front two positions.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Finish Through Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong enough that hold-up horses can find daylight and close in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: If the pace is genuinely strong enough that hold-up horses can find daylight and close in the final furlong.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Wide-Open Blanket Finish
scenarios.trigger: If the field races in a tight bunch with no runner securing a tactical advantage and multiple horses finishing within a length.
scenarios.body: If the field races in a tight bunch with no runner securing a tactical advantage and multiple horses finishing within a length.

watchPoints.text: Space Bear (Appleby/Mason) gets away cleanly — if she leads by two lengths after two furlongs unchallenged, she is controlling this race and the entire field is chasing her terms.

Monitor Frantic (Downing) and Sugar Baby (Winn) in the opening furlong — if either pushes forward aggressively to press Space Bear, the pace lifts materially and the shape shifts toward Scenario B, significantly altering which horses are favoured.

Emperor Caradoc (Nolan) is the most dangerous closer in the field given three wins on this going at this course; watch whether Nolan can find a clear passage from the hold-up position, as a muddled mid-pack will bury his chance entirely.

Taygar (Kirrane) has seven places on Good 6f ground but has yet to win; if the field bunches and gaps appear late, it will be finishing — but in a controlled pace it is likely to run another respectable but unrewarded race.

Tactical Formation returns from 166 days off — watch the betting market move for confirmation the Fahey yard has it ready; if it drifts in the market, the absence concern is real and it can be safely discounted.

runners_data.name: It Just Takes Time

runners_data.name: Degale
runners_data.note: Hold-up operator who stays well and is effective in good ground over 7f-8f; the step back in trip from his recent starts is worth noting but the style needs more pace than this setup is likely to generate.

runners_data.name: Ormolulu
runners_data.note: Consistent hold-up performer whose sole placed run in good going (3rd at 6f) came over a shorter trip; needs pace to draw on, which this race shape may not supply in sufficient quantity.

runners_data.name: Woodstock
runners_data.note: Naturally prominent-racing type who has run consistently from the front rank on good ground at 7f-8f, but the field's congestion at the head of affairs means she's unlikely to secure her ideal spot; headgear (p) worn, which has been part of her recent profile.

runners_data.name: Mr King
runners_data.note: Hold-up racer who fades in the finish and has been running over longer trips (8f-10f); dropping to 7f is interesting but the ⚠ fade flag and an 0/15 recent record in good going make him hard to back.

runners_data.name: Gressington

runners_data.name: Inside Story
runners_data.note: Prominent-running 3-year-old with in-form handler James Tate (5 wins from 14 in 14 days); only 2 runs in good going limits the sample, but the step up to 7f from shorter trips is untested in good conditions and the 35-day absence is worth monitoring.

runners_data.name: Zarvali
runners_data.note: Progressive 3-year-old prominent racer with excellent good-going form (6 runs all on good, won once, placed twice); recent win at 7f good is directly relevant and Roger Fell in fair form.

runners_data.name: Fuji Mountain
runners_data.note: A true hold-up horse whose redistribution to midfield reflects the volume of closers in this field; best form at 5f on good ground, so the step up to 7f is a significant question, and the claiming jockey (3lb) adds uncertainty.

runners_data.name: City Captain
runners_data.note: Listed as NON-RUNNER — disregard entirely from all calculations.

runners_data.name: This Farh
runners_data.note: Lightly-weighted prominent racer with headgear (p) and three wins from 15 in good/similar going; the 1/8f winning form on good ground is slightly longer than today's 7f but the in-running headgear and 10-day return make him a legitimate pace-scenario beneficiary.

races.paceDynamic: Kosometsuke is the confirmed front-runner here and, with no genuine rival for the lead, is set to control this 7f Thirsk contest from the front at a comfortable, sustainable gallop. The field contains a cluster of prominent types — It Just Takes Time, Zarvali, Inside Story, and Woodstock — who will press into the early positions behind the leader, but none profiles as a horse who will force a truly searching pace. This creates the conditions for a steady-to-fair gallop through the first half of the race, with the tempo only picking up in the final quarter-mile, which is the critical phase on this track. The race shape strongly favours horses who can travel prominently or make progress from mid-division once the pace quickens, rather than true closers who need a fast early gallop to generate momentum late. Woodstock, Gressington, and Fuji Mountain are genuine prominent or hold-up types redistributed to midfield because the field holds more forward-going runners than can realistically occupy those positions, with Kosometsuke, It Just Takes Time, and Zarvali most likely to actually secure the prominent berths.

watchPoints.text: Kosometsuke has a clear lead but the style-fit flag (0.93) is live — watch whether Connor Beasley allows a fully uncontested gallop or whether It Just Takes Time and Zarvali push up harder than expected in the early stages, which could compromise the front-runner's chance of lasting home.

Zarvali has won over 7f in good going and has the form profile to sit second or third throughout; if he travels smoothly in behind Kosometsuke and produces a clean run through, he is the most dangerous prominent challenger in Scenario B.

This Farh has won three of his last six starts and wears headgear; watch whether he can find a prominent position from his draw, because if he secures a tracking role he has the profile to finish off strongly in the final furlong when the pace lifts.

Gressington and Fuji Mountain are both true closers redistributed to midfield; if the race develops any significant early pace, keep an eye on whether either can make late progress, but note that the sustainable-pace forecast makes this unlikely rather than probable.
City Captain is listed as a non-runner — confirm non-runner status at the declaration stage, as removal reduces the field to 11 and marginally eases the competition for prominent positions.

runners_data.name: Hover On The Wind
runners_data.note: Paul Midgley yard has had two winners in the last 14 days and this six-year-old has placed on Tapeta but lacks convincing Good-ground form (sim-going strike rate 9/15, 1W); held up naturally but the map places it forward of where it wants to be, limiting its realistic chance here.

runners_data.name: Khabib
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old who has placed four times at 5f on Good without winning; a genuine prominent racer whose natural role has been squeezed out by the cluster of pace types, meaning it may face a trip further back than ideal — headgear (p) noted but Good-ground win record is absent.

runners_data.name: Le Beau Garcon
runners_data.note: Back quickly after just five days rest, Michael & David Easterby yard clocking three winners in 14 days; has a place on Good at 5f and a win on it last year, and Joanna Mason's claim is relevant — this is a hold-up type with a legitimate late-run profile if the pace softens.

runners_data.name: Beaumadier
runners_data.note: 84 days off the track is the significant flag here; Mark Loughnane's yard is winless in the past 14 days and Hope Regan claims seven pounds, which helps the weight but is a combination that asks questions; ran respectably on Tapeta but no Good-turf win in the formbook.

runners_data.name: Military Girl
runners_data.note: Two wins from three starts on Good at 5f, Connor Beasley booked and Michael Dods yard in form with three winners in 14 days — the profile fits this pace shape as well as anything in the race, sitting prominent and punching at the line.

runners_data.name: Spendmore Lane
runners_data.note: The confirmed pace-setter with early-speed/stamina headgear flag (e/s) and a consistent front-running profile; Good-turf form is limited (2/15 sim-going, 0W1P) which is the one genuine concern, and the STYLE_FIT tag reflects it may not fully control the race if pushed — but no rival is likely to do that here.

runners_data.name: Emerald Harmony
runners_data.note: David Nolan partners this Paul Midgley hold-up type; placed three times on Good at 5f and twice on Soft, showing consistent finishing — needs the pace to lift and hold-up horses to be given a run, which this shape only partly facilitates.

runners_data.name: King's Crown
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with headgear (tp) and six consecutive placed or mid-field finishes without a win; Good-turf sim-going record is poor (2/15, 0W1P) and the form string of 556653 indicates a horse that competes without winning, making it a frame rather than a win candidate here.

races.paceDynamic: Spendmore Lane is the confirmed lone front-runner here, carrying early-pace mandate on a flat, fair 5f Good surface at Thirsk where leaders with a clear run routinely hold on. With no genuine challenger for the lead, Spendmore Lane can dictate at a controlled, sustainable tempo rather than being dragged into a scrap — this is the critical distinction. Military Girl, Beaumadier, and King's Crown are all legitimate prominent types who will push into the first two or three lengths behind, creating a compact early group but not a true pace war. The field holds more hold-up and prominent types than the map can accommodate in their natural positions: Khabib, Pal Joey, and Hover On The Wind are genuine front-of-field or hold-up horses redistributed to midfield, meaning those slots behind Spendmore Lane will likely be contested by Military Girl, Beaumadier, and King's Crown instead. With an uncontested lead and an honest but not extreme pace, this race shape strongly favours prominent racers who travel just behind the leader and kick — horses like Military Girl who want to be on the pace and have the form on Good ground are ideally placed, while true hold-up horses face a tough ask unless something goes wrong up front.

scenarios.title: Lone Leader Controls

scenarios.body: If Spendmore Lane bowls clear unopposed and sets a steady-to-honest tempo that plays to prominent types sitting just off the pace.

scenarios.body: If Spendmore Lane sets a pace that proves too hot to sustain and ties up in the final furlong, releasing hold-up runners from off the pace.

scenarios.body: If Military Girl, Beaumadier, or King's Crown push aggressively early and force a contested pace battle behind Spendmore Lane.

scenarios.body: If multiple pace positions are contested, the field fans wide, and none of the obvious protagonists travel fluently.

watchPoints.text: Military Girl has won twice on Good at 5f in her last four starts and Connor Beasley rides for a yard that has sent out three winners in the past fortnight — watch for her to sit second or third and maintain a challenge all the way to the line.
Spendmore Lane's ability to get a clear, uncontested lead is the fulcrum of the entire race — if it jumps cleanly and is allowed to stride away, the result may already be settled by halfway.

Le Beau Garcon returns after just five days rest with Joanna Mason claiming — watch the betting market closely as a strong move here, given the Easterby yard's current form, could signal stable confidence in a horse with a genuine Good-ground profile.

Beaumadier's 84-day absence combined with a 7lb claimer and no recorded Good-turf win is a combination worth monitoring if it drifts in the market — fitness on return is unproven and the yard is cold.

Khabib and Pal Joey are both operating out of their natural race positions due to pace congestion — watch whether either is able to secure a prominent berth at the break, as doing so would improve both their chances materially versus their mapped positions.

races.paceDynamic: Crocus Time is the confirmed lone front-runner here, and on a flat, straight 5f at Thirsk in Good conditions, an uncontested lead over 11 rivals is a significant tactical advantage — this horse has won three of its last five and arrives in form. The remainder of the field is overwhelmingly made up of hold-up and prominent types, with Knicks, Midnight Lir, Blue Lakota, Albegone, and Invincible Crown all natural hold-up horses who cannot all settle into their preferred rear position and are redistributed forward on the map. Irish Dancer and Startling are the most likely prominent challengers to push toward the early pace, though neither has the profile to seriously disrupt Crocus Time's rhythm from the front. This race shape heavily favours the front-runner and horses with early pace who can race prominently, as there is no genuine rival to force a contested, lung-burning gallop — closers will likely face a wall of horses ahead and a steady pace they cannot adequately accelerate past.

watchPoints.text: Crocus Time's early lead is the race-shaping factor — watch whether Irish Dancer or Startling (if running) pushes forward at the break, because any sustained pressure in the first two furlongs would significantly alter this race shape and reduce Crocus Time's winning probability.|
Startling carries a non-runner jockey flag — confirm the replacement ride before the off, as the change of pilot on a prominent-style runner could affect how aggressively it seeks position early.|

Dandy Dinmont's trainer Nigel Tinkler is 0 from 24 over the last 14 days, a form-of-yard concern that should temper enthusiasm for a horse that otherwise has solid course-and-distance form on Good going.|

Blue Lakota's 29-day absence and minimal Good-ground form (0 wins, 0 places from 3 runs) makes it a horse to treat cautiously despite Kevin Ryan's overall strength as a trainer — its natural hold-up style is the worst fit for the anticipated race shape.|

The cluster of redistributed hold-up horses — Knicks, Midnight Lir, Albegone, Invincible Crown, Blue Lakota — will all be competing for the same ground in the final furlong; watch for traffic issues and interference in the closing stages if the field concertinas behind Crocus Time.|
